field_summary:
WASHINGTON, March 28, 2025 – Cargill Kitchen Solutions, a company in Lake Odessa, Michigan, is recalling approximately 212,268 pounds of liquid egg products that may contain a cleaning solution with sodium hypochlorite, announced today the Food Safety and Inspection Service (FSIS) of the US Department of Agriculture.

The liquid egg products were produced on March 12-13, 2025. The following products are subject to recall:

  • 32 oz. (2 lb.) carton containing ‘egg beaters ORIGINAL LIQUID EGG SUBSTITUTE’ and 'USE BY' date 10 AUG 2025.
  • 32 oz. (2 lb.) carton containing ‘egg beaters CAGE-FREE ORIGINAL LIQUID EGG SUBSTITUTE’ and 'USE BY' date 09 AUG 2025.
  • 32 oz. (2 lb.) carton containing ‘egg beaters CAGE-FREE ORIGINAL FROZEN EGG SUBSTITUTE’ and 'USE BY' date 07 AUG 2026.
  • 32 oz. (2 lb.) carton containing ‘Bob Evans Better'n Eggs Made with Real Egg Whites’ and 'USE BY' date 10 AUG 2025.

The recalled products are marked with the establishment number 'G1804' printed in ink on the carton. These products were shipped to distributors in Ohio and Texas and for use in food service establishments in Arizona, California, Colorado, Florida, Illinois, and Iowa. There is a possibility that these products have been distributed nationally.

The problem was discovered when FSIS received information about potential contamination of these products. After conducting an investigation and a thorough evaluation of the cleaning solution contents, FSIS scientists concluded that the use of this product would not cause adverse health effects or pose a significant risk, so a Class III recall is being conducted.

Although FSIS does not expect adverse health effects from recalled Class III products and has not received confirmed reports of adverse reactions due to consumption of these products, anyone with concerns about illness should contact a healthcare provider.

FSIS is concerned because some of the product may be in consumers' refrigerators or freezers. Consumers who purchased these products are urged not to consume them and food service establishments are urged not to serve them. These products must be discarded or returned to the point of purchase.

FSIS conducts routine reviews of recall effectiveness to verify that companies conducting a recall notify their customers and follow necessary steps to ensure the product is no longer available to consumers.

Consumers and media with questions about the recall can contact Chuck Miller, Cargill Kitchen Solutions, at 1-844-419-1574 or media@cargill.com.

Consumers with questions about food safety can call the USDA's Meat and Poultry Hotline at 888-MPHotline (888-674-6854) or send an email to MPHotline@usda.gov. Consumers who need to report a problem with meat, poultry, or egg products can access the Electronic Consumer Complaint Form 24 hours a day at https://foodcomplaint.fsis.usda.gov/eCCF/.
